name: 2s/10s Yield Curve Inversion → S&P 500 Peak & Drawdown
description: Analyzes each 2s/10s yield curve inversion event (spread crosses below zero). For each inversion: marks the event, computes the subsequent S&P 500 peak over the next 504 trading days (~2 years), estimates the lag from inversion to peak, and calculates the maximum drawdown from that peak. Uses T10Y2Y spread from FRED and SP500 index level. Outputs: yield curve spread chart with inversion shading, event markers on each inversion, and a summary table with per-event metrics.
source:
# --- 2s/10s Yield Curve Inversion → S&P 500 Peak & Drawdown ---
# Detects each inversion start (spread crosses below 0), then computes:
#   - S&P 500 level at inversion
#   - Subsequent S&P 500 peak (max over next 504 trading days)
#   - Lag from inversion to that peak (days)
#   - Max drawdown from peak (trough / peak - 1) over next 504 days

# --- Data ---
src = study_assets()()
ts = index().value

# FRED: 2s/10s spread and S&P 500 level
spread_raw = economic_indicators(series_id="T10Y2Y")().result
spx_raw = economic_indicators(series_id="SP500")().result

# Forward-fill for dense series
spread = ffill(spread_raw)
spx = ffill(spx_raw)

# --- Inversion Detection ---
# Inversion starts when spread crosses below zero
inversion_start = crossunder(spread, 0)

# Track inversion regime (spread < 0)
in_inversion = hold_until(enter=spread < 0, exit=spread >= 0)

# --- Forward-Looking Metrics at Each Inversion Start ---
# S&P 500 level at inversion
spx_at_inv = where(inversion_start, spx)

# Forward max over next 504 trading days (~2 years) from each bar
# We compute rolling max of FUTURE prices using lead shifts
# Max of S&P over next 63/126/252/378/504 trading days
fwd_max_63 = agg(spx << 1, 63, AggregationType.Max)
fwd_max_126 = agg(spx << 1, 126, AggregationType.Max)
fwd_max_252 = agg(spx << 1, 252, AggregationType.Max)
fwd_max_378 = agg(spx << 1, 378, AggregationType.Max)
fwd_max_504 = agg(spx << 1, 504, AggregationType.Max)

# The overall peak in the 2-year window after inversion
fwd_peak = agg(spx << 1, 504, AggregationType.Max)

# Forward min over next 504 trading days (to find trough after peak)
fwd_min_504 = agg(spx << 1, 504, AggregationType.Min)

# Estimate lag to peak: find which horizon first reaches the 2-year max
# If max_63 == peak, lag ~63 days; if max_126 == peak, lag ~126 days, etc.
# We use the earliest horizon that achieves the peak
peak_at_inv = where(inversion_start, fwd_peak)
min_at_inv = where(inversion_start, fwd_min_504)

# Estimate peak lag: check which forward window first captures the peak
lag_est_63 = where(inversion_start, fwd_max_63)
lag_est_126 = where(inversion_start, fwd_max_126)
lag_est_252 = where(inversion_start, fwd_max_252)
lag_est_378 = where(inversion_start, fwd_max_378)
lag_est_504 = where(inversion_start, fwd_max_504)

# Approximate lag in trading days to peak
# If peak reached within 63d window → ~63d, within 126d → ~126d, etc.
peak_lag = where(inversion_start, conditional_select(
    fwd_max_63 == fwd_peak, 63,
    fwd_max_126 == fwd_peak, 126,
    fwd_max_252 == fwd_peak, 252,
    fwd_max_378 == fwd_peak, 378,
    504
))

# Return from inversion to peak
inv_to_peak_ret = where(inversion_start, (fwd_peak - spx) / spx)

# Max drawdown from peak = (trough - peak) / peak
# This is the worst decline from the highest point in the 2-year window
max_dd = where(inversion_start, (fwd_min_504 - fwd_peak) / fwd_peak)

# --- Event Markers: Each Inversion Start ---
event_marker(
    schema=EventMarkerSchema(
        title='Yield Curve Inversion',
        icon=Icon.AlertTriangleIcon,
        schemas=[
            ColumnSpec(title='2s/10s Spread', dp=2, type=CardRenderType.DecimalFormat,
                       card_slot=CardSlot.Hero),
            ColumnSpec(title='S&P 500 Level', dp=0, type=CardRenderType.IntegerFormat,
                       card_slot=CardSlot.Subtitle),
            ColumnSpec(title='Est. Days to Peak', dp=0, type=CardRenderType.IntegerFormat,
                       card_slot=CardSlot.Details),
            ColumnSpec(title='Max Drawdown from Peak', dp=1, type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat,
                       card_slot=CardSlot.Footer),
            ColumnSpec(table_is_filter=True, table_visible=False)
        ]
    )
)(where(inversion_start, spread), spx_at_inv, peak_lag, max_dd, inversion_start)

# --- Chart 1: Yield Curve Spread with Inversion Shading ---
# Show spread over time with zero reference and inversion regime as band
inv_flag = where(in_inversion, 1, 0)

xy_lines(
    title='When Does the Yield Curve Invert?',
    y_axis_label='2s/10s Spread (%)',
    category='Yield Curve Inversion Analysis',
    order=1,
    series=LineSeriesSchema(series=[
        LineSeriesSpec(name='2s/10s Spread', color=Color.Blue),
        LineSeriesSpec(name='Inverted', color=Color.Red, is_band=True)
    ]),
    reference_lines=ReferenceLineSchema(lines=[
        ReferenceLine(value=0, title='Zero', color=Color.Gray, dash_style=DashStyle.Dash)
    ])
)(ts, spread, inv_flag)

# --- Chart 2: S&P 500 Return from Inversion to Peak ---
# Bar chart showing how much S&P gained from inversion to its subsequent peak
xy_bars(
    mode=BarMode.series,
    agg=AggregationType.Mean,
    title='How Much Does the S&P Rally Before the Crash?',
    y_axis_label='Inversion → Peak Return',
    y_axis_format=CardRenderType.PercentFormat,
    category='Yield Curve Inversion Analysis',
    order=2,
    data_labels=True,
    color_by_value=True,
    series=BarSeriesSchema(series=[
        BarSeriesSpec(name='Avg Return to Peak', color=Color.Blue),
        BarSeriesSpec(name='Avg Max Drawdown', color=Color.Red)
    ]),
    reference_lines=ReferenceLineSchema(lines=[
        ReferenceLine(value=0, title='Zero', color=Color.Gray, dash_style=DashStyle.Dash)
    ])
)(inv_to_peak_ret, max_dd)

# --- Table: Per-Event Detail ---
summary_table(
    mode=TableMode.standard,
    category='Yield Curve Inversion Analysis',
    order=3,
    layout=SummaryTableLayout(
        title='Inversion Events: S&P 500 Peak & Drawdown',
        row_size=1, col_size=6,
        col_headers=['N Events', 'Median Days to Peak', 'Median Return to Peak', 'Median Max DD', 'Worst Max DD', 'Best Return to Peak'],
        cells=[
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=0, grid_agg=AggregationType.Count,
                       type=CardRenderType.IntegerFormat, dp=0),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=1, grid_agg=AggregationType.Median,
                       type=CardRenderType.IntegerFormat, dp=0),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=2, grid_agg=AggregationType.Median,
                       type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=3, grid_agg=AggregationType.Median,
                       type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=4, grid_agg=AggregationType.Min,
                       type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1),
            ColumnSpec(grid_row=0, grid_col=5, grid_agg=AggregationType.Max,
                       type=CardRenderType.PercentFormat, dp=1)
        ]
    )
)(peak_lag, peak_lag, inv_to_peak_ret, max_dd, max_dd, inv_to_peak_ret)
